decision:
SPINE: Proposal 2 (shipping) — its milestone ordering is the only one that survives contact with this repo, because it lands the ledger as a pure library before any route and puts the wallet last. GRAFTS: Proposal 1's schema (promo/purchased account split, holds-as-accounts, dated jurisdiction rows, policy_decisions logging allows-as-well-as-denies) and Proposal 3's single best idea, DETERMINISTIC ENTRY PRIMARY KEYS DERIVED FROM THE IDEMPOTENCY KEY — which is the actual answer to the flaw that every judge landed on.

THE SHARED FATAL FLAW, AND THE FIX. All three proposals build the ledger write as one `db.batch()` whose guards are `WHERE version=?` clauses, and all three claim `meta.changes` aborts the batch. It does not. D1 rolls a batch back when a statement ERRORS; an UPDATE matching zero rows is a SUCCESSFUL statement returning changes:0, and the batch commits. The `compareSwap` precedent they all cite (duel-service.mjs:230-239) works only because it is ONE statement, so a miss means nothing was written. That property does not survive generalisation to a 6-statement batch: the entry INSERTs commit while the balance UPDATE no-ops, and because the same designs forbid UPDATE/DELETE on ledger_entries and pin UNIQUE(idem_key), the corruption is unrepairable and the retry errors on the idempotency index. On proposal 1's own rule the reconciler then hard-stops the money layer on the first contended stake.

THE RULE THIS PLAN IS BUILT ON: inside a D1 batch, only an exception rolls back, so every guard must be expressible as a constraint violation. Three mechanisms, layered, no `meta.changes` inspection anywhere in the ledger: (1) tx_id and entry_id are derived as sha256(op_key || ':' || leg_index), so a REPLAY collides on PRIMARY KEY and errors; (2) UNIQUE(account_id, seq) with seq = entry_seq+1 read at the top of the request, so a LOST RACE collides and errors — this is optimistic concurrency whose failure is an exception, not a row count; (3) CHECK (flags & 1 = 0 OR credits_cached - debits_cached >= 0) on ledger_accounts, so an OVERDRAFT raises. Double-spend becomes structurally impossible rather than transactionally prevented, which is the correct posture on a platform with no interactive transactions.

SECOND SHARED FLAW: NO SCHEDULER EXISTS, AND ONE CANNOT BE DECLARED HERE. Verified: the deploy manifest is generated from .openai/hosting.json ({"d1":"DB","r2":null}) through localBindingConfig at vite.config.ts:19-37, and the generated dist/server/wrangler.json reads triggers:{}, kv_namespaces:[], queues:{producers:[],consumers:[]}, durable_objects:{bindings:[]}, r2_buckets:[]. There is no wrangler.toml. Proposals 1 and 2 rest five money-safety jobs (hold expiry, settlement sweep, idempotency completer, reconciliation, anon deletion) on a cron that has nowhere to run; proposal 2 piggybacks them on "the same bounded cleanup batch as room expiry", and that batch has exactly one caller — the create path (duel-service.mjs:478) — so a player's stake sits past expiry until somebody starts a new duel. FIX: no money invariant may depend on a background job. Settlement is synchronous in the request that terminates the room; holds are enforced opportunistically by any later request touching the account; and the reconciler runs from .github/workflows/sweep.yml (a schedule: cron in the one scheduler this repo can actually declare) against an authenticated /api/ops route — which also supplies the admin surface for the kill switch that no proposal provided, despite declaring policy_flags.updated_by NOT NULL with no writer.

THIRD SHARED FLAW: THE BOT SEAT CANNOT HOLD A STAKE. attachBot writes players[1] = { hash: null, kind: 'bot' } — no principal, no ledger account — while readyPlayer debits r.balances for BOTH seats and settleMatch credits balances[winner] which may be the bot. Every proposal's settle intent requires two funded accounts. normalizeConfig validates opponent and stake independently (room-engine.mjs:36-38), STAKES [0,10,25,50,100] is user-selectable at match-settings.tsx:112, and duel-client-static.ts:65 permits ONLY bot duels — so staked bot duels are the only duel the live GitHub Pages deployment has. FIX: ledger-backed staking requires two principals; bot rooms are stake-0 on the ledger path, enforced by a coupling in normalizeConfig, and add_bot is refused on a ledger-staked room.

FOURTH: THE OUTBOX ORDERING IS FALSE. "Write the outbox row in the same compareSwap batch" does not cover the common case — a duel that ends on the final answer settles through commitAttempt (duel-service.mjs:551); compareSwap (:561) is reached only when !newReveal && !newAnswer. FIX: act on a guarded write that RETURNED a row (proof it landed), then post settlement with deterministic key settle:<roomId>. No co-committed outbox.

FIFTH, AND THE BIGGEST SIMPLIFICATION: THE PROFILE NEVER CHANGES. All three proposals bump profile v2→v3, and judges correctly identified passport.mjs:62 as the most destructive line in the repo. Proposal 1's "ship the upgrader in a release that does nothing else" is unachievable — wallet.gems is read at 10 sites across lib/progression.mjs and app/, and readProgression's documented "Identity on valid state" property (which transactProfile's output !== before write-skip depends on) must survive the rename. FIX: server-held value NEVER enters the profile blob. Gems stay device-local, offline-earnable, cosmetic-only, worth nothing — exactly as today. Server Coins are a ledger balance the device has no schema slot for, cached in a separate IndexedDB object store. passport.mjs:62 is never touched, the version stays 2, no legacy import, no cap, no hostile-claim path, and the 247 tests keep passing. The device credential also goes in that separate store, never the profile, because exportAll (use-player.ts:238-263) downloads the profile unfiltered to disk.

TWO LEDGERS, NOT ONE (from proposal 2). ledger='play' is free, server-authoritative, non-purchasable, non-withdrawable. ledger='value' is purchasable and disabled everywhere by default. lib/ledger/posting.mjs refuses any transaction whose entries do not all share the transaction's ledger, so "payments are off" is an invariant of a pure function, not a flag anyone must remember. Cash-in is two ledger-partitioned transactions sharing an external_ref, never one spanning both.

POLICY BEFORE VALUE (from proposal 3). The jurisdiction engine ships at M1, before there is anything to gate, and every money-shaped request logs a policy_decisions row from then on — so the gate accumulates months of production evidence before it guards a cent. Rules are dated D1 rows with a citation and a named reviewer; default-deny on an unlisted region; India carries a scheduled 2026-05-01 successor row with paid_entry=0 and purchase=0 while play=1, so the entire free-to-play product keeps running there and the prohibition lands without anyone remembering to ship. KV is not rejected on philosophical grounds — it is simply not bound in this deployment, which forces the D1-only choice all three proposals argued for anyway.

milestones.name: Platform truth and harness atomicity
milestones.delivers: The two things every later milestone silently assumed and none of them verified: a test harness whose batch() is a real transaction, and a scheduler that exists. Today tests/d1-local.mjs implements batch as Promise.all(statements.map(s => s.run())) with no transaction at all, and with yieldIO:true every run() awaits setImmediate() first, so two concurrent batches interleave statement-by-statement. Any ledger concurrency test written against that harness passes for the wrong reason. Separately, dist/server/wrangler.json is generated with triggers:{}, kv_namespaces:[], queues:{...empty}, durable_objects:{bindings:[]} — there is nowhere in this repo to declare a cron, a queue consumer or a DO. This milestone establishes the scheduler the repo CAN declare (a GitHub Actions schedule: workflow calling an authenticated route) and the ops/admin surface that the kill switch needs in order to be a control rather than a paragraph.
milestones.schema: Migration 0002: ops_runs(run_id TEXT PK, kind TEXT NOT NULL, started_at INTEGER NOT NULL, finished_at INTEGER, outcome TEXT, detail TEXT, heartbeat_at INTEGER NOT NULL) + ops_runs_kind_idx ON (kind, started_at DESC). This is the dead-man's switch substrate: a sweep that stops running stops writing heartbeats, and silence becomes detectable rather than indistinguishable from health.
invariants: A batch containing a statement that raises leaves ZERO rows written — assert by running a batch of [good INSERT, constraint-violating INSERT] and querying for the first row's absence.

A batch containing a zero-row guarded UPDATE does NOT roll back its siblings — assert the sibling INSERT DID land. This test exists to pin the exact semantics the whole ledger design is betting on, so a future platform change breaks a test rather than the books.
Within one batch, statements do not interleave with another concurrent batch, even with yieldIO:true.
LocalD1.batch rejects on the first statement error and rolls back via ROLLBACK.
MemoryRoomStore.batch applies every statement with no await between the first guard and the last write, matching the header contract already documented at lib/duel-memory-store.mjs:1-15.
/api/ops rejects a request whose secret does not match env.OPS_SECRET under constant-time comparison, and never echoes the secret in any response body or error.
A sweep run writes exactly one ops_runs row whose outcome is set, even when the sweep itself throws.
milestones.doneWhen: node --test tests/*.test.mjs is 247 + new and green; tests/d1-batch-semantics.test.mjs pins both the rollback-on-error and the no-rollback-on-zero-rows cases; .github/workflows/sweep.yml runs on a schedule and a manual dispatch, and a no-op sweep has been observed writing an ops_runs heartbeat in a real deployment; docs/money-runbook.md names who is paged, the first three steps after a hard stop, and who can clear it. pnpm build:static unchanged.

milestones.name: Jurisdiction policy engine and honest disclosure
milestones.delivers: The per-jurisdiction runtime decision, shipped before anything exists to gate, so the gate accumulates real production traffic and a real decision log before it guards a cent. Rules are dated rows, not build constants: India's 1 May 2026 prohibition is a scheduled successor row with play=1 and paid_entry=0/purchase=0, so the entire free-to-play product keeps running there and the prohibition takes effect without a deploy. An unlisted US subdivision inherits the most restrictive country default, so a new state ban is a non-event — you only ever ADD permissions. Independently valuable as a shipped honesty feature even if no wallet ever exists: rules-screen.tsx:173-176 stops quoting a hardcoded claim and starts quoting the resolved decision with its reasons. The kill switch is an authenticated /api/ops call from M0, not an imagined SQL snippet, and policy_flags.updated_by finally has a writer.
milestones.schema: Migration 0003: jurisdiction_rules(region TEXT NOT NULL, effective_from INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to INTEGER, play INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, paid_entry INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, purchase INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, cash_out INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, min_age INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 18, max_daily_purchase_minor INTEGER, citation TEXT NOT NULL, reviewed_at INTEGER NOT NULL, reviewed_by TEXT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (region, effective_from)); policy_flags(key TEXT PK, value TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL, updated_by TEXT NOT NULL, reason TEXT); policy_decisions(id TEXT PK, principal_id TEXT, at INTEGER NOT NULL, region TEXT NOT NULL, region_source TEXT NOT NULL, question TEXT NOT NULL, answer INTEGER NOT NULL, reason TEXT NOT NULL, rules_version TEXT NOT NULL, op_key TEXT) + decisions_at_idx, decisions_principal_idx. Seeded: one '*' row that is all zeros except play=1; 'IN' with a 2026-05-01 successor carrying paid_entry=0/purchase=0; the ~12 cash-entry-blocked US states as US-XX rows. policy_flags seeded payments_master='off'.
invariants: An unknown region denies everything except play, with reason 'no_rule_deny'. Default-deny is structural: the resolver returns deny when no row matches, it does not fall through to a permissive default.
Most-specific-wins: 'US-WA' beats 'US' beats '*'.
'IN' flips at exactly 2026-05-01T00:00:00Z and permits paid entry the millisecond before under the prior row.
payments_master='off' overrides every permissive row — the flag is a deny-only term and can never turn a capability ON. All 8 combinations of (code default, rule answer, flag) pinned as a table.
An expired effective_to denies.
Absent request.cf resolves to an unknown region and therefore denies — which is what the static build and local dev look like.
lib/server/region.mjs contains no reference to cf-connecting-ip and never persists or returns an IP; asserted by source grep.
Every money-shaped evaluation writes a policy_decisions row INCLUDING the allows. Allows-as-well-as-denies is what makes this evidence rather than a log.
resolve() is pure: same bundle plus same subject yields a byte-identical decision and the same decision hash.
milestones.doneWhen: tests/policy-engine.test.mjs snapshots the full region x question truth table so a rule edit that changes behaviour shows up as a test diff; a kill-switch drill through /api/ops is timed end to end and the number is written into docs/money-runbook.md; the static build answers the policy action with the all-denied offline decision and its banner copy is asserted; rules-screen.tsx renders resolved policy text rather than a constant.

milestones.name: Ledger core as a pure library — no route, no table, no I/O
milestones.delivers: The hardest correctness work in the project, as pure .mjs reducers in the house style, testable under node:test beside the existing 247 with zero infrastructure. Double-entry is enforced at the API boundary: you cannot express a money move without naming both sides, and lib/ledger/posting.mjs throws before anything touches a database. The ledger partition is enforced here, which is what makes 'payments are off by default' an invariant of a pure function rather than a flag: no code path, not even a buggy one, turns a free play coin into a purchasable one, because the planner would have to emit a cross-ledger transaction and it refuses. Deterministic id derivation also lands here, as a pure function, so the structural anti-double-post property is unit-tested before any store exists.
milestones.schema: None. Deliberately no migration and no route — this milestone is provable with zero infrastructure, which is what makes the later wiring a wiring exercise rather than a design exercise.
invariants: Every transaction has at least two entries and sum(debits) === sum(credits); posting.mjs throws LedgerError otherwise.
All entries share the transaction's ledger; a cross-ledger posting is refused. Asserted for every intent in the closed set.
amount is always a positive integer in minor units and direction carries the sign — never a float, never a signed amount, never a decimal string.
entryId(opKey, legIndex) is deterministic, collision-resistant across leg indices, and stable across processes; the same intent replayed produces byte-identical ids.
A client-initiated intent may not name a system-only account path (house, psp, bank, liability, revenue).

Property test: 10,000 random intents against a random account set, asserting the trial balance after EVERY step, not only at the end — a bug that transiently creates value for one step is still a bug.
No intent can move value from a play account to a value account or back, under any argument combination.

Funding preference: holdStake spends promo/free origin before purchased origin, always, and records the split on the hold so a release restores the original proportions rather than laundering promo into purchased.
invariants.mjs exports the same assertion functions the production reconciler will call — that identity is the point, and is asserted by both files importing the same module.
milestones.doneWhen: ~60 new node:test cases green; the 10,000-intent property test runs in CI on every commit; every rejection reason is a named test; lib/ledger/ has zero imports of anything with I/O, asserted by source grep. Suite ~247 → ~305. pnpm build:static unchanged.

milestones.name: Ledger persisted — constraint-guarded, both stores, no meta.changes anywhere
milestones.delivers: The ledger in D1 and in memory, with every guard expressed as a constraint violation so D1's batch rolls back for the reason it actually rolls back. This is the milestone that fixes the flaw all three proposals shared. A post is one db.batch() of: INSERT ledger_transactions (deterministic tx_id → replay collides on PK → error), INSERT ledger_entries per leg (deterministic entry_id → replay collides on PK; lost race collides on UNIQUE(account_id, seq) → error), and one UPDATE per touched ledger_accounts row carrying the cached balance and entry_seq (overdraft trips a CHECK → error). Every failure mode is an exception; nothing inspects meta.changes. The cached balance is Square Books' decision taken deliberately — a wallet screen that GROUP BYs a growing entry log is the exact scaling failure Block wrote up, and D1 gives 1,000 queries and 30s per invocation.
milestones.schema: Migration 0004. ledger_accounts(account_id TEXT PK (colon path), ledger TEXT NOT NULL, kind TEXT NOT NULL, normal TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(normal IN ('debit','credit')), owner_principal_id TEXT, flags INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, debits_cached INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, credits_cached INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, entry_seq INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, opened_at INTEGER NOT NULL, closed_at INTEGER, CHECK (flags & 1 = 0 OR credits_cached - debits_cached >= 0), CHECK (flags & 2 = 0 OR debits_cached - credits_cached >= 0)). ledger_transactions(tx_id TEXT PK (=sha256(op_key)), op_key TEXT NOT NULL, ledger TEXT NOT NULL, code TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, ref_kind TEXT, ref_id TEXT, rules_version TEXT NOT NULL, region TEXT NOT NULL, sum_debit INTEGER NOT NULL, sum_credit INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_at INTEGER NOT NULL, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, reverses_id TEXT, timeout_at INTEGER, CHECK (sum_debit = sum_credit), CHECK (sum_debit > 0)). ledger_entries(entry_id TEXT PK (=sha256(op_key||':'||leg_index)), tx_id TEXT NOT NULL, account_id TEXT NOT NULL, direction TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(direction IN ('debit','credit')), amount INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(amount > 0), ledger TEXT NOT NULL, seq INTEGER NOT NULL, leg_index INTEGER NOT NULL, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL) + UNIQUE INDEX entries_account_seq_uq ON (account_id, seq) + entries_tx_idx. ledger_holds(hold_id TEXT PK, account_id, ledger, source_split TEXT NOT NULL, amount INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(amount>0), state TEXT NOT NULL, purpose TEXT NOT NULL, ref_kind TEXT NOT NULL, ref_id TEXT NOT NULL, expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL, hold_tx_id TEXT NOT NULL, resolve_tx_id TEXT, UNIQUE(purpose, ref_kind, ref_id, account_id)) + holds_active_expiry_idx. money_ops(op_key TEXT NOT NULL, principal_id TEXT NOT NULL, route TEXT NOT NULL, request_hash TEXT NOT NULL, recovery_point TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'started', locked_until INTEGER, attempts INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, response_status INTEGER, response_body TEXT, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (principal_id, op_key)) + idem_incomplete_idx. ledger_checkpoints(ledger, window_to, account_id, debits, credits, entry_count, digest, PRIMARY KEY(ledger, window_to, account_id)). Plus two triggers on ledger_entries: BEFORE UPDATE and BEFORE DELETE, each SELECT RAISE(ABORT,'ledger_entries is append-only').
invariants: A replayed post writes nothing and errors on the tx PRIMARY KEY — double-posting is impossible by index, independent of batch semantics, retries, or two Workers racing. Assert by issuing the identical op_key twice and counting entry rows.

Two interleaved posts against one account: exactly one commits, and THE LOSER WROTE NOTHING. This is the assertion every proposal omitted — proposal 1's stated test only checks that one wins. Assert entry count and tx count, not just the balance.
An overdraft on a flags&1 account raises and the whole batch rolls back — no tx row, no entry rows, no balance movement.
An UPDATE or DELETE against ledger_entries raises, enforced by trigger at the SQLite level, not by convention or by grep alone.
CHECK (sum_debit = sum_credit) rejects an unbalanced transaction at the storage layer, so 'no value was created' is answered by a constraint before it is answered by a code review.
For every account, entry_seq === COUNT(entries) and cached debits/credits === SUM(entries); seq is contiguous 1..N with no gaps.

Per ledger, sum of credit-normal balances equals sum of debit-normal balances — AND no individual account is on the wrong side of its own flags. A negative held account satisfies the global identity arithmetically, so the global check alone is not sufficient; proposal 2's reconciler would have reported balanced books on a corrupt ledger.

The reconciler is INCREMENTAL: it scans entries after the last ledger_checkpoints watermark, with a hard per-invocation statement cap well under D1's 1,000, and seals a window on success. A full re-derivation of a 10M-row entry log cannot run in a Worker and must not be the design.
The same scenario suite passes against both LedgerStoreD1 (over the now-transactional LocalD1) and the memory store, the way tests/duel-memory.test.mjs already holds three room stores equivalent.
No file under lib/ledger/ or lib/server/ledger-store-d1.mjs references meta.changes — source grep.
milestones.doneWhen: tests/schema-constraints.test.mjs proves each CHECK, each UNIQUE and both triggers reject at the SQLite level; the loser-wrote-nothing concurrency test is green against LocalD1 with yieldIO on; the reconciler runs from the M0 sweep workflow against a seeded database and writes a checkpoint; injecting each corruption from the invariants fixtures makes the run fail and name the right invariant. lib/server/ledger-store-d1.mjs carries a header stating the batch rule.

milestones.name: Principals — silent anonymous identity, promotion without re-keying
milestones.delivers: A server-minted principal created silently on first server contact, so there is a stable subject for every device long before anyone signs in, and promotion to a named account is an INSERT against the SAME principal_id — nothing in the ledger, the holds or the entitlements ever moves. This is Firebase's linkWithCredential guarantee reproduced with two SQL statements, and it is why identity must live in the same D1 as the ledger: hosted auth would make every promotion and every merge a distributed operation across exactly the boundary Kleppmann says not to cross. The duel hot path is deliberately NOT changed to resolve a principal: polling is 500ms per seat against a single-threaded ~1,000 q/s instance pinned to first-primary, so adding a sessions SELECT to every poll would roughly double primary reads and halve concurrent capacity — a cost two judges flagged and no proposal budgeted. Only money-shaped requests resolve a principal. The device secret goes in a NEW IndexedDB object store, never in the profile, because exportAll (use-player.ts:238-263) downloads the profile unfiltered to disk and a bearer credential must never land there.
milestones.schema: Migration 0005: principals(principal_id TEXT PK (32 hex, reusing the existing validId regex at duel-service.mjs:45), kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'anon', display_name TEXT, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, promoted_at INTEGER, session_epoch INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, merged_into TEXT, home_region TEXT, region_source TEXT, age_band TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unknown', status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active', status_reason TEXT); principal_devices(secret_hash TEXT PK, principal_id TEXT NOT NULL, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, last_seen_at INTEGER NOT NULL, revoked_at INTEGER); principal_identities(provider TEXT NOT NULL, subject TEXT NOT NULL, principal_id TEXT NOT NULL, email_hash TEXT, linked_at INTEGER NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (provider, subject)). The composite PK on principal_identities IS the credential-already-in-use detector; session_epoch is the whole revocation mechanism, so bumping one column invalidates every live token for that principal with no sessions table on the hot path.
invariants: Promotion preserves principal_id exactly; no foreign key anywhere is rewritten. Assert by taking a full row census before and after.

Linking a credential that already belongs to another principal returns 409 with a merge token and WRITES NOTHING — never an auto-merge, because silent merging is where every implementation of this loses someone's value.

A merge is a ledger transaction: merge_transfer postings move value promo→promo and purchased→purchased, never laundering one into the other; the orphan is marked merged_into and RETAINED, so both histories survive and the transfer is visible in both statements forever.
A merge is refused while either principal holds an active hold.
Bumping session_epoch invalidates every outstanding token for that principal.
The device secret never appears in the profile blob and therefore never appears in the exportAll download — asserted by round-tripping a real export and grepping it.
No response body ever contains a session token, a device secret, a raw email or a principal_id — mirroring tests/http.test.mjs:49-52, which already pins that projections never leak correctIndex.
The duel route issues ZERO additional D1 reads per poll; the actor derivation at http-handler.mjs:65-69 upgrades to the device secret hash, which costs the same hash it already computes.

Shared-handset rule: a genuinely different principal on this device discards local wholesale and replaces from the server; the same principal resuming does a union merge. One player's progress can never leak into the next person's.
/api/account is rate-limited; {action:'hello'} is an unbounded row-creation endpoint on the same D1 that holds the ledger and must carry its own admission budget.
milestones.doneWhen: tests/http-account.test.mjs mirrors tests/http.test.mjs case for case (cross-origin 403, oversized 413, missing DB 503, forged token 401, expired token 401); the static build refuses every account action with the existing 501 offline_build error and a CI grep asserts dist-static/ contains no '/api/account'; pnpm build:static green; 247 original tests untouched and passing.

milestones.name: Free-play economy becomes server-authoritative
milestones.delivers: Editing IndexedDB stops minting anything the server recognises, and — the real point — the exact code path that money will later use runs in production under precisely zero financial risk. Server Coins are granted only for events the server durably observed, keyed on server-minted identifiers: round.id (already `${r.id}:${r.roundIndex}` at room-engine.mjs, beginRound) and roomId. This is the correction to proposal 1's contradiction, which claimed grants come from server-observed facts and then proposed keying them on deriveEvents journal ids — ids minted client-side in lib/journal.mjs, which is handing the client the mint. XP, levels, streaks, badges, quests, conviction tiers, the journal, the Vault, expeditions and analytics all stay on the device, fully earnable offline, worth nothing — a player who edits to level 99 gains a number, not a thing anyone paid for, and the disclosure copy says so rather than pretending otherwise. Ledger staking is an ADDITIVE room config (ledgerStake), so the existing balances:[1000,1000] demo economy in the room blob is untouched and the static build keeps working exactly as it does today — the flaw that broke proposal 2's equivalent milestone.
milestones.schema: Migration 0006: matches(room_id TEXT PK, ledger TEXT NOT NULL, stake INTEGER NOT NULL, mode TEXT NOT NULL, duration INTEGER NOT NULL, seat0_principal TEXT, seat1_principal TEXT, seat1_is_bot INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, bot_disclosed INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, funding TEXT NOT NULL, region0 TEXT NOT NULL, region1 TEXT, rules_version TEXT NOT NULL, state TEXT NOT NULL, winner_seat INTEGER, reason TEXT, deck_commit TEXT NOT NULL, settle_posted INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, settled_at INTEGER) + matches_unsettled_idx ON (settle_posted, created_at) WHERE settle_posted=0 + per-principal indexes. entitlements(principal_id, sku, granted_at, source, ledger_tx_id, revoked_at, PRIMARY KEY(principal_id, sku)). The matches row is INSERTed at stake time, not at settle time — a recovery queue written by the operation it exists to recover cannot recover anything.
invariants: A ledger-staked room requires two principals. normalizeConfig refuses opponent==='bot' with stake>0 on the ledger path, and attachBot refuses a ledger-staked room, closing the add_bot hole where a bot can be attached to an already-funded friend room.

Free-play rooms are byte-identical to today: makeRoom still mints balances:[1000,1000], readyPlayer still debits both seats, settleMatch still credits balances[winner]. All 247 existing tests pass unchanged and the static build still runs staked bot duels.

Settlement is posted from a guarded write that RETURNED a row — proof it landed — never co-committed with a compareSwap that may lose its race. The deterministic key settle:<roomId>:<winner_seat>:<reason> means a contradictory second settlement surfaces as a visible conflict rather than being swallowed as a replay.

A decided match is never silently voided: the hold expirer refuses to void a hold whose ref_id has a matches row with a non-null winner_seat. Refunding both sides of a completed duel because a sweep beat the settle is worse than the lag it was meant to fix.
No grant intent accepts a client-supplied identifier. Source-grep asserted, plus a behavioural test that a forged journal id mints nothing.

XP never converts to Coins on any path; expedition confidence tiers mint no currency (extending the existing pin at tests/betting-audit.test.mjs:205 from a game-balance control to a compliance control).

seat1_is_bot and bot_disclosed are RECORDED facts, not rendered ones, and projection().players[].kind still exposes bot opposition. Skillz won $420M against Papaya for advertising human opponents while matching against bots; once value is attached, a matchmaking claim is evidence.

rooms.state is validated on every JSON.parse (duel-service.mjs:454, :473, :485, :550, :561) by a pure total validator. Today that blob is unvalidated and safe only because the server is its sole writer — not good enough once a matches row references it.

Room blob carries a schemaVersion with a dual-read branch: rooms live 2 hours, so a deploy that changes the blob shape must not throw a TypeError on in-flight rooms and bypass the GameError status mapping at http-handler.mjs:76-88.
Every settled duel has exactly one capture or release per seat; every staked duel has exactly two active-or-resolved holds.
milestones.doneWhen: End-to-end duels across all five settle reasons (complete, timing-inconsistent, room-expired, player-not-connected, player-left) against both stores; a chaos test that kills the process between the room write and the settle post, asserting the next request to that room converges and never captures twice; pnpm build:static green with a staked bot duel still settling; leaderboards derived from ledger entries rather than device claims.

milestones.name: Payment seam and value ledger — provider-null in production, full arc in CI
milestones.delivers: The complete purchase → stake → settle → refund → reverse → reconcile path, demonstrable end to end to a processor's underwriting team, to a regulator or to an investor, with no merchant account and no cent. Production runs provider-null: every purchase attempt returns 503 payments_disabled. selectProvider requires BOTH payments_master='on' AND a provider secret actually bound, so a leaked flag alone cannot enable payments and a leaked secret alone cannot either. The value ledger exists and is disabled; no principal has a value balance and there is no migration path from play to value, because posting.mjs throws on a cross-ledger transaction. Purchase credits are NEVER posted before the provider confirms — you do not credit coins you have not been paid for. This is the last milestone that needs no legal clearance, and it is where the jurisdiction gate from M1 starts being enforced on a real code path rather than a hypothetical one.
milestones.schema: Migration 0007: provider_events(event_id TEXT PK — the provider's own id, so a redelivery is an INSERT OR IGNORE that changes nothing, provider TEXT NOT NULL, kind TEXT NOT NULL, received_at INTEGER NOT NULL, signature_ok INTEGER NOT NULL, payload_sha256 TEXT NOT NULL, processed_at INTEGER, ledger_tx_id TEXT, outcome TEXT) + pev_unprocessed_idx WHERE processed_at IS NULL. orders(order_id TEXT PK, principal_id TEXT NOT NULL, sku TEXT NOT NULL, currency TEXT NOT NULL, amount_minor INTEGER NOT NULL, state TEXT NOT NULL, provider_ref TEXT, rules_version TEXT NOT NULL, region TEXT NOT NULL, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL). The value ledger rows are seeded disabled, so a posting to a fiat ledger is refused by a flag long before any provider exists.
invariants: Every interface method of provider-null throws and maps to 503 through the EXISTING error mapper at http-handler.mjs:76-88 — no new status mapping.
selectProvider returns the null provider when the flag is on but no secret is bound, AND when a secret is bound but the flag is off. Both directions pinned.

Idempotency, one named test per failure mode from the research brief: duplicate on retry; lost charge via a reused key with different params (422, never a silent replay of the old result); cross-user key collision (the unique index is scoped by principal); concurrent double-submit against a live lease (409, never cached); a cached 4xx that was actually retriable (validation failures and lease conflicts are NOT cached); retry storm without jitter; and the indeterminate timeout against a provider whose capabilities().supportsIdempotency is false — marked permanently failed, never blind-retried.
A stored response replays byte-identically INCLUDING a stored 500, so a replayed failure replays as a failure.

Recovery points advance started → ledger_posted → provider_called → finished, each committed WITH that phase's data. Local intent commits BEFORE any foreign call, never inside a transaction wrapping it, because a foreign state mutation cannot be rolled back.
A duplicate webhook, an out-of-order webhook (success arriving after refund) and a bad-signature webhook each leave the ledger balanced and the op key in a terminal state.
Downstream keys derive from ours as factduel-<op_key> so our idempotency composes with the provider's rather than competing with it.
Cash-in is two ledger-partitioned transactions sharing a ref, never one spanning both; a single transaction touching two ledgers is refused by the pure planner.

The completer's own health is a ledger invariant: the reconciler counts ops older than ten minutes still short of 'finished' and trips the kill switch above a threshold. A completer running on a scheduler that silently stopped is otherwise indistinguishable from a completer with nothing to do.
No response body and no logged op key contains PII — op keys are logged, so they are UUIDs, never emails.
milestones.doneWhen: tests/payments-seam.test.mjs runs the complete arc against the sandbox provider on EVERY commit — buy, stake, settle with rake, refund, reverse, reconcile — asserting balanced books and zero drift at every step, and the same arc with policy denying purchase asserts that nothing whatsoever is written; a kill-switch drill stops purchases within the measured window with no redeploy; the first clean reconciliation report is archived as the artefact underwriting will ask for.

milestones.name: Real money, one jurisdiction
milestones.delivers: A real provider binding, ONE jurisdiction_rules row flipped to purchase=1 with a citation and a named reviewer, and max_daily_purchase_minor set low so the worst single-account exposure is small. By construction this is the smallest milestone of the eight: no code changes from M6, because everything hard already shipped. It is a binding swap and a policy INSERT. India is not this region and cannot be — its dated row carries purchase=0 and paid_entry=0 from 2026-05-01 and the resolver will refuse regardless of what anyone flips. GATED: this milestone is the ONLY one that requires legal clearance, because it is the only one where a cent moves. Everything from M0 to M6 takes no money, stakes no real value, and is mergeable and shippable on engineering judgement alone.
milestones.schema: Migration 0008 is a data-only seed: one jurisdiction_rules INSERT for the cleared region, carrying the legal citation in citation and the reviewer's name in reviewed_by. No DDL. Enabling a market is an INSERT of a dated row, never an UPDATE of an existing one, so every past decision stays reproducible and a rollback is an effective_to edit rather than a deploy.
invariants: The sandbox provider's entire contract suite passes against the real provider's test mode, in a MANUALLY triggered workflow — never in the default node --test tests/*.test.mjs run, so CI never depends on a third party.

The payment instrument's country must agree with the stored region or the purchase is refused and the principal is flagged. Geo-IP is a gate, not proof; being wrong in the permissive direction is the expensive kind, and instrument agreement is the second of three layers.
Age gating is evaluated for the first time here. No birthdate is collected before this point — collecting one before you need it is a liability, not a feature.

cash_out remains 0 in every row including '*'. The ledger supports it structurally and nothing implements it, because cash-out is what converts 'game with purchasable currency' into 'gambling operator' across most of these jurisdictions and drags in KYC, AML, sanctions screening, segregated client funds and unclaimed-property escheatment.

A user-visible balance is backed by a real credit-normal liability account funded from a real cash account. HQ Trivia's most visible failure was unpaid winners, not the prize economics: a balance not backed by segregated, reconciled funds is a liability, not a feature.
milestones.doneWhen: LEGAL SIGN-OFF RECORDED IN jurisdiction_rules.reviewed_by. Engineering preconditions, all independently verifiable: the M3 reconciler has run clean for 30 consecutive days; a kill-switch drill has been timed end to end and the number is in the runbook; an operator has reconstructed every movement for one principal from ledger_entries alone with no application code involved; and the on-call rotation, alert thresholds and post-hard-stop clearance procedure are written down and rehearsed.

rejected: Durable Objects for rooms — rejected on proposal 2's grounds AND on a harder one nobody checked: DO bindings are not declarable in this deployment. The generated manifest reads durable_objects:{bindings:[]} and migrations:[], and .openai/hosting.json exposes only d1 and r2. Moving rooms to DOs would also destroy the D1RoomStore/MemoryRoomStore/LocalD1 three-way equivalence that tests/duel-memory.test.mjs and the entire static build depend on. Proposal 1's judge recommended DOs as the fix for the batch-atomicity flaw; the constraint-based fix in M3 solves it without leaving D1, which matters because the ledger must stay in the same database as principals, policy and idempotency keys.

Cloudflare Queues — not bound (queues:{producers:[],consumers:[]}) and not declarable here. Independently: at-least-once delivery is the wrong semantics for the write a user's balance reads back, and proposals 1 and 2 both put settlement behind a queue whose consumer has nowhere to run. Settlement is synchronous in the request that terminates the room, with a deterministic key making reattempt free.

KV for the kill switch and the nonce store — kv_namespaces:[] in the generated manifest, so this is moot, but the design reasons stand. KV is eventually consistent with ~1 write/s per key and no read-your-writes, and proposal 1's 'nonce seen-once in KV' cannot be seen-once at all: two concurrent replays in different colos both read 'unseen'. The seen-once primitive is the money_ops INSERT under its unique index.

Guarding a D1 batch with meta.changes on a WHERE version=? clause — the shared fatal flaw. A zero-row UPDATE is a successful statement and the batch commits, leaving entries written and balances stale, in the ordinary two-tabs-two-stakes case. Replaced by constraint-based guards where every failure is an exception.

Hosted auth (Clerk, Auth0, Firebase, WorkOS) — the principal row and the ledger's account rows must be in the same database and the same batch, or guest→named promotion and account merge become cross-system distributed operations, with the failure mode of a user named in one system and anonymous in the other while holding value. All three proposals reached this conclusion independently and all three are right.

Profile v2→v3, the wallet→walletCache rename, and the legacy gem import — rejected wholesale. passport.mjs:62 silently discards a version mismatch, wallet.gems is read at 10 verified sites across lib/progression.mjs and app/, and readProgression's documented 'Identity on valid state' property (which transactProfile's output !== before write-skip depends on) would have to survive the rename. Proposal 1's 'ship the upgrader in a release that does nothing else' is not achievable as written. Making server value never touch the profile blob removes the migration, the cap, the hostile-claim path, the R2 evidence blobs and the highest-risk line in all three plans, at the cost of one honest sentence in the UI: Gems are yours and offline; Coins are on the server.

An outbox row co-committed with compareSwap — false for the path that actually settles most duels. A duel ending on the final answer commits through commitAttempt (duel-service.mjs:551); compareSwap (:561) is reached only when !newReveal && !newAnswer. Worse, a batched outbox INSERT commits even when the CAS loses its race, emitting settlement intents for room writes that never happened — and the deterministic key then makes the phantom authoritative.
match_records inserted at settle time — a recovery queue written by the operation it exists to recover cannot recover anything. The row is inserted at stake time with settle_posted=0.

Cash-out in any form at any milestone — may_cash_out stays 0 in every row including the wildcard. The ledger supports it structurally (the liability and operating accounts exist) and nothing implements it.

An offline queue for money intents — an offline stake is simply unavailable with honest copy, not queued. An offline money queue means reconciling conflicting wallet state on reconnect, which is the hardest problem in the design, bought for a feature nobody asked for.

Drizzle at runtime — getDb() has zero callers today and keeps having zero. The ledger needs batch() with constraint-guarded statements whose exceptions it must distinguish by index name, which an ORM obscures. Drizzle stays generation-only, which is also what makes tests/d1-local.mjs's journal replay keep working with no loader edit.
openRisks: THE BATCH-ROLLBACK SEMANTICS ARE A PLATFORM BEHAVIOUR, NOT A CONTRACT WE CONTROL. This plan bets that D1 executes a batch as a transaction and rolls it back on statement error. Every guard in M3 is designed to fail as an exception for exactly that reason. Re-verify against live docs at implementation time — the engineering brief itself flags that Cloudflare's limits and pricing moved in January 2026. tests/d1-batch-semantics.test.mjs exists so a change breaks a test rather than the books, and lib/ledger/store-contract.mjs is the abstraction boundary that would let the ledger move behind a single-threaded store if batch ever stops being transactional.

THE SCHEDULER IS A GITHUB ACTIONS CRON, WHICH IS BEST-EFFORT. Actions schedules can be delayed by minutes to hours under load and are disabled on repositories with no activity for 60 days. This is why no money invariant may depend on it: settlement is synchronous, holds are enforced opportunistically by any later request touching the account, and the sweep is a backstop plus a reconciler, not a correctness component. If .openai/hosting.json ever gains a triggers slot, move the sweep to a real Cron Trigger — but do not make the design depend on that happening.

NOBODY ON THE TEAM HAS RUN A LEDGER, AND THE FAILURE MODE IS SILENT. A subtly wrong posting does not throw; it makes the books wrong and you find out months later. The whole M2/M3 stance is the mitigation — the CHECK constraints, the append-only triggers, the property test asserting trial balance after every single intent, and the incremental reconciler sharing its assertion functions with the test suite. Build the reconciler at M3, before the payment seam at M6, not after.

D1 THROUGHPUT IS THE CEILING, NOT D1 STORAGE. Single-threaded at roughly 1,000 q/s, shared with the room table, and the client polls at 500ms while active. This plan keeps the duel hot path free of any new D1 read specifically to protect that budget, but the number is unmeasured — README.md:98-104 already names observed capacity and error budgets as a known gap. Measure before M5 ships ledger staking, and state the q/s budget per concurrent duel.

READ REPLICATION IS A DOUBLE-SPEND WINDOW IF USED CARELESSLY, AND THE SESSION IS PER-STORE. D1RoomStore calls withSession('first-primary') in its constructor (duel-service.mjs:186); a separately constructed ledger store over the same env.DB gets an INDEPENDENT session with an independent bookmark, so the room commit and the ledger post have no read-your-writes relationship. Construct ONE session per request in the ingress and pass the handle into both stores. This cannot be caught by a unit test and must be a code-review gate.

D1 TIME TRAVEL IS A WHOLE-DATABASE RESTORE AND IS ACTIVELY DANGEROUS HERE. The ledger shares one binding with live rooms, so a bad ledger deploy has no rollback that does not also rewind duels and the rate limiter — and restoring rewinds money_ops alongside ledger_transactions, so every webhook and retry arriving afterwards re-executes against keys that no longer record their first execution. The restore becomes a double-post event on the very table that prevents them. Until a separate database or an R2 export exists, any Time Travel restore requires quarantining the provider first; write that into the runbook at M0, not at M7.

GEO-IP IS WRONG FOR VPN USERS AND BEING WRONG PERMISSIVELY IS THE EXPENSIVE DIRECTION. A player in a banned state on a VPN who is allowed to purchase is the exact fact pattern that produces an enforcement action. Fail closed on unknown regions, treat a client-declared region as narrowing only, require instrument-country agreement at M7, and keep max_daily_purchase_minor low at launch.

LEGAL FACTS MOVE FASTER THAN CODE AND THE SCHEMA CANNOT CREATE A REVIEW CADENCE. The dated rows with citation and reviewed_by make an unreviewed market impossible to enable anonymously, but a named owner and a calendar are not engineering artefacts. This is the single highest-risk non-engineering dependency in the plan.

THE ENTIRE OBSERVABILITY STORY IS ONE WORKFLOW AND ONE TABLE. The generated manifest gives observability:{enabled:true}, which buys Workers Logs and nothing more; there is no metrics sink, no alert channel and no on-call rotation in this repo. Every failure this design introduces is silent by construction — value resting in holds, unsettled matches accumulating, ops stuck short of 'finished', drift nobody reads. The four counters and the pager must be named at M0 or the kill switch is a control that can stop the money layer but cannot wake anyone.
REFUSING A MERGE MID-DUEL PRODUCES A CONFUSING USER-FACING ERROR. This is correct and should stay. Accept the confusing error for the handful of people who hit it; do not build the clever version.

GRANT RATES FOR SERVER COINS ARE UNSPECIFIED AND ARE A PRODUCT DECISION, NOT AN ENGINEERING ONE. M5 establishes that grants are keyed on round.id and roomId and bounded by a per-principal daily cap, but which server-observed events mint how much is a balance question that needs product sign-off before M5 ships. Related and worth getting sign-off on early: offline play stops earning the staking currency. That is a real product regression and must be stated plainly in the UI rather than papered over with a sync that would be forgeable.
